data.name: Artemus
data.gender_notes: Artemus is used as a male name in christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The meaning of Artemus is recorded in name-lists as “Man's man, butcher, protector”. This meaning has NOT been verified against a classical lexical or onomastic source, so it is published as an unverified candidate only. The record is flagged for manual source verification.
data.spiritual_meaning: Artemus expresses “Man's man, butcher, protector”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Artemus total 25, reducing to 7. Number 7 is associated with reflection, analysis and inner search.

in_hebrew.name: ערטמוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the root 'artem' meaning 'two' and 'maseh' meaning 'strong'.

in_greek.name: Αρτέμος
in_greek.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek goddess Artemis, meaning 'butcher', 'hunter', 'goddess of wilderness', or 'goddess of the hunt'. In the New Testament, it is the name of a disciple of Jesus.

in_latin.name: Artemus
in_latin.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'Artemis', which is a translation of the Greek goddess Artemis.

data.cultural_impact: Artemus is used in Biblical naming tradition with the meaning “Man's man, butcher, protector”.

biblical_reference.note: Artemas was a disciple of Jesus and a companion of St. Luke. He was probably the same person as the one named Drusus in Acts 16:1, and was possibly the bearer of the letter from the church at Ephesus to Paul in Acts 27:1-26.
